Abstract & How to Use This Manual

This Is a condensed version of the Master Reference Sheet. This physics establishes that macroscopic cosmology, localized quantum mechanics, and solid-state phenomena evaluate as the deterministic consequences of continuum mechanics operating within a dynamic elastic vacuum. By defining the uncurled metric as a compressible, refractive fluid, the foundations of physical law are systematically derived from classical fluid dynamics, Eulerian material derivatives, and geometric topology.

  • PART I provides the dynamically numbered Cheat Sheet containing the raw equations for quick use and reference.

  • PART II [Click Here] provides explicit, step-by-step mathematical proofs from first principles.

  • The [Proof ↓\downarrow] links in each box navigate directly to the corresponding formal derivation.

Absolute energy evaluates as the displaced fluid volume of the continuous metric. Potential and kinetic energies evaluate as physical, geometric partitions of the localized total scalar admittance (αs\alpha_s).

PHASE IV: WAVE KINEMATICS & ELECTROMAGNETISM

The Unified Fluid Lagrangian & Modal Admittance

The continuous mechanics of the metric evaluate as a unified thermodynamic fluid action. Because the Helmholtz decomposition partitions the total kinematic field into orthogonal geometries, the fluid metric evaluates as an anisotropic viscoelastic tensor governed by Modal Admittance.

1. The Absolute Kinematic Capacity (vtot2≤c2v_{tot}^2 \le c^2):
The total fluid velocity vector partitions into three orthogonal driving fields: the longitudinal scalar gradient (∇h\nabla h), the transverse vector circulation (∇×𝐀\nabla \times \mathbf{A}), and the localized internal topological vorticity (∇×𝐯ψ\nabla \times \mathbf{v}_{\psi}).

Because the longitudinal scalar gradient evaluates irrotational fluid compression, it tracks the kinematic velocities driven by both the ambient macroscopic volume pressure (Gravity, ∇𝒫ambient\nabla \mathcal{P}_{ambient}) and the localized dynamic surface pressure (Propulsion, ∇𝒫local\nabla \mathcal{P}_{local}). The total squared velocity (vtot2v_{tot}^2) evaluates the localized kinematic capacity of the medium, bounded by c2c^2: vtot2=(∇h)2+(∇×𝐀)2+(∇×𝐯ψ)2≤c2v_{tot}^2 = (\nabla h)^2 + (\nabla \times \mathbf{A})^2 + (\nabla \times \mathbf{v}_{\psi})^2 \le c^2 \tag{93}Equation (93) In the macroscopic vacuum, the kinematic velocity evaluates near zero (vtot2≪c2v_{tot}^2 \ll c^2). Where the kinematic fields maximize, the fluid saturates the capacity limit (vtot2→c2v_{tot}^2 \to c^2).

2. Modal Admittance (αi\alpha_{i}) & Fluid Compliance:
Because the kinematic components strain the fluid in orthogonal dimensions, they consume the absolute phase-space limit (cc) independently. The fluid admittance evaluates as a discrete modal limit for each geometric strain: α∥=1−(∇h)2c2α⟂=1−(∇×𝐀)2c2α↺=1−(∇×𝐯ψ)2c2\begin{aligned} \alpha_{\parallel} &= \sqrt{1 - \frac{(\nabla h)^2}{c^2}} \nonumber \\ \alpha_{\perp} &= \sqrt{1 - \frac{(\nabla \times \mathbf{A})^2}{c^2}} \nonumber \\ \alpha_{\circlearrowleft} &= \sqrt{1 - \frac{(\nabla \times \mathbf{v}_{\psi})^2}{c^2}} \tag{94} \end{aligned}Equation (94)

3. Topological Confinement (The Infinite Deborah Number):
The Deborah number (DeDe) defines the phase transition between fluid compliance and solid rigidity. As geometric compliance (α\alpha) drops to zero, the structural relaxation time diverges (De→∞De \to \infty).

Where the internal rotational velocity saturates the medium (|∇×𝐯ψ|→c|\nabla \times \mathbf{v}_{\psi}| \to c), the rotational admittance mathematically vanishes: |∇×𝐯ψ|→c⟹α↺→0⟹Derot→∞|\nabla \times \mathbf{v}_{\psi}| \to c \implies \alpha_{\circlearrowleft} \to 0 \implies De_{rot} \to \infty \tag{95}Equation (95) Where rotational compliance evaluates to zero, the metric loses capability to yield to shear and behaves as a rigid solid. Because macroscopic translational velocities remain below the kinematic limit ((∇h)2≪c2(\nabla h)^2 \ll c^2), translational admittances remain open (α∥≈1\alpha_{\parallel} \approx 1). A continuous field evaluates as an unyielding solid exclusively in its saturated axis.

4. The Localized Compliance Limit:
Squaring the modal admittances and summing their states reveals the viscoelastic geometry: Σαi2=(1−(∇h)2c2)+(1−(∇×𝐀)2c2)+(1−(∇×𝐯ψ)2c2)Σαi2=3−vtot2c2\begin{aligned} \Sigma \alpha_i^2 &= \left(1 - \frac{(\nabla h)^2}{c^2}\right) + \left(1 - \frac{(\nabla \times \mathbf{A})^2}{c^2}\right) + \left(1 - \frac{(\nabla \times \mathbf{v}_{\psi})^2}{c^2}\right) \nonumber \\ \Sigma \alpha_i^2 &= 3 - \frac{v_{tot}^2}{c^2} \tag{96} \end{aligned}Equation (96) Evaluating this sum where the kinematic capacity saturates (vtot→cv_{tot} \to c): Σαi2=3−c2c2=2\Sigma \alpha_i^2 = 3 - \frac{c^2}{c^2} = 2 \tag{97}Equation (97) To maintain the phase limit, the localized metric possesses two fully compliant degrees of kinematic freedom; the saturated dimension structurally freezes (α=0\alpha = 0) as an energetic boundary.

5. The Dynamic Field Lagrangian (ℒdynamic\mathcal{L}_{dynamic}):
The dynamic action evaluates the kinetic energy density (𝒦\mathcal{K}) minus the structural potential energy density (𝒫\mathcal{P}).

The kinetic energy evaluates as the sum of the orthogonal velocity strains scaled by respective modal admittances: 𝒦=12ρτ[α∥(∇h)2+α⟂(∇×𝐀)2+α↺(∇×𝐯ψ)2]\mathcal{K} = \frac{1}{2} \rho_{\tau} \Big[ \alpha_{\parallel}(\nabla h)^2 + \alpha_{\perp}(\nabla \times \mathbf{A})^2 + \alpha_{\circlearrowleft}(\nabla \times \mathbf{v}_{\psi})^2 \Big] \nonumber

The structural potential energy consists of the absolute macroscopic vacuum tension (ρτc2\rho_{\tau} c^2) and the localized topological acoustic cavitation (12ρτc2\frac{1}{2} \rho_{\tau} c^2). The absolute structural potential (𝒫\mathcal{P}) evaluates as the difference: 𝒫=ρτc2−12ρτc2=12ρτc2\mathcal{P} = \rho_{\tau} c^2 - \frac{1}{2} \rho_{\tau} c^2 = \frac{1}{2} \rho_{\tau} c^2 \nonumber

Subtracting the potential energy from the kinetic energy constructs the field Lagrangian: ℒdynamic=12ρτ[α∥(∇h)2+α⟂(∇×𝐀)2+α↺(∇×𝐯ψ)2]−12ρτc2\mathcal{L}_{dynamic} = \frac{1}{2} \rho_{\tau} \Big[ \alpha_{\parallel}(\nabla h)^2 + \alpha_{\perp}(\nabla \times \mathbf{A})^2 + \alpha_{\circlearrowleft}(\nabla \times \mathbf{v}_{\psi})^2 \Big] - \frac{1}{2} \rho_{\tau} c^2 \tag{98}Equation (98)

6. The Absolute Kinematic Lagrangian (ℒkin\mathcal{L}_{kin}):
To isolate the pure geometric action of the phase space, the absolute background mass density (ρτ\rho_{\tau}) is factored out of the dynamic Lagrangian.

Dividing the dynamic Lagrangian by ρτ\rho_{\tau} mathematically annihilates the mass term, yielding the Absolute Kinematic Lagrangian in native spatiotemporal dimensions (m2/s2\text{m}^2/\text{s}^2): ℒkin=12[α∥(∇h)2+α⟂(∇×𝐀)2+α↺(∇×𝐯ψ)2]−12c2\mathcal{L}_{kin} = \frac{1}{2} \Big[ \alpha_{\parallel}(\nabla h)^2 + \alpha_{\perp}(\nabla \times \mathbf{A})^2 + \alpha_{\circlearrowleft}(\nabla \times \mathbf{v}_{\psi})^2 \Big] - \frac{1}{2} c^2 \tag{99}Equation (99) The geometric action of the continuum evaluates exclusively as scale-invariant phase-space evolution, independent of the numerical magnitude of the macroscopic fluid density.

7. The Universal Angular Phase-Space Lagrangian:
Defining the total velocity vtotv_{tot} via spherical coordinates extracts the geometric phase space for any arbitrary magnitude: (∇h)2=vtot2cos⁡2(θ)(∇×𝐀)2=vtot2sin⁡2(θ)cos⁡2(ϕ)(∇×𝐯ψ)2=vtot2sin⁡2(θ)sin⁡2(ϕ)\begin{aligned} (\nabla h)^2 &= v_{tot}^2 \cos^2(\theta) \nonumber \\ (\nabla \times \mathbf{A})^2 &= v_{tot}^2 \sin^2(\theta)\cos^2(\phi) \nonumber \\ (\nabla \times \mathbf{v}_{\psi})^2 &= v_{tot}^2 \sin^2(\theta)\sin^2(\phi) \nonumber \end{aligned}

Substituting these continuous velocity components into the Modal Admittances yields the dynamic compliance states: α∥=1−vtot2c2cos⁡2(θ)α⟂=1−vtot2c2sin⁡2(θ)cos⁡2(ϕ)α↺=1−vtot2c2sin⁡2(θ)sin⁡2(ϕ)\begin{aligned} \alpha_{\parallel} &= \sqrt{1 - \frac{v_{tot}^2}{c^2} \cos^2(\theta)} \nonumber \\ \alpha_{\perp} &= \sqrt{1 - \frac{v_{tot}^2}{c^2} \sin^2(\theta)\cos^2(\phi)} \nonumber \\ \alpha_{\circlearrowleft} &= \sqrt{1 - \frac{v_{tot}^2}{c^2} \sin^2(\theta)\sin^2(\phi)} \nonumber \end{aligned}

Substituting these explicit angular components back into the Kinematic Lagrangian (ℒkin\mathcal{L}_{kin}) factors the total kinematic intensity (vtot2v_{tot}^2) from the topology. Writing the full explicit expansion reveals the pure geometric phase space of the continuous fluid: ℒkin(vtot,θ,ϕ)=12vtot2[1−vtot2c2cos⁡2(θ)cos⁡2(θ)+1−vtot2c2sin⁡2(θ)cos⁡2(ϕ)sin⁡2(θ)cos⁡2(ϕ)+1−vtot2c2sin⁡2(θ)sin⁡2(ϕ)sin⁡2(θ)sin⁡2(ϕ)]−12c2\begin{aligned} \mathcal{L}_{kin}(v_{tot}, \theta, \phi) = \frac{1}{2} v_{tot}^2 \Big[ &\sqrt{1 - \frac{v_{tot}^2}{c^2} \cos^2(\theta)} \cos^2(\theta) \nonumber \\ &+ \sqrt{1 - \frac{v_{tot}^2}{c^2} \sin^2(\theta)\cos^2(\phi)} \sin^2(\theta)\cos^2(\phi) \nonumber \\ &+ \sqrt{1 - \frac{v_{tot}^2}{c^2} \sin^2(\theta)\sin^2(\phi)} \sin^2(\theta)\sin^2(\phi) \Big] \nonumber \\ &- \frac{1}{2} c^2 \tag{100} \end{aligned}Equation (100)

28. The Unified Fluid Lagrangian & Modal Admittance

vtot2=(∇h)2+(∇×𝐀)2+(∇×𝐯ψ)2≤c2α∥=1−(∇h)2c2,α⟂=1−(∇×𝐀)2c2,α↺=1−(∇×𝐯ψ)2c2|∇×𝐯ψ|→c⟹α↺→0⟹Derot→∞Σαi2=3−vtot2c2vtot→c⟹Σαi2=2ℒdynamic=12ρτ[α∥(∇h)2+α⟂(∇×𝐀)2+α↺(∇×𝐯ψ)2]−12ρτc2ℒkin=12[α∥(∇h)2+α⟂(∇×𝐀)2+α↺(∇×𝐯ψ)2]−12c2ℒkin(vtot,θ,ϕ)=12vtot2[1−vtot2c2cos⁡2(θ)cos⁡2(θ)+1−vtot2c2sin⁡2(θ)cos⁡2(ϕ)sin⁡2(θ)cos⁡2(ϕ)+1−vtot2c2sin⁡2(θ)sin⁡2(ϕ)sin⁡2(θ)sin⁡2(ϕ)]−12c2\begin{aligned} v_{tot}^2 &= (\nabla h)^2 + (\nabla \times \mathbf{A})^2 + (\nabla \times \mathbf{v}_{\psi})^2 \le c^2 \tag{93} \\ \alpha_{\parallel} &= \sqrt{1 - \frac{(\nabla h)^2}{c^2}}, \quad \alpha_{\perp} = \sqrt{1 - \frac{(\nabla \times \mathbf{A})^2}{c^2}}, \quad \alpha_{\circlearrowleft} = \sqrt{1 - \frac{(\nabla \times \mathbf{v}_{\psi})^2}{c^2}} \tag{94} \\ |\nabla \times \mathbf{v}_{\psi}| &\to c \implies \alpha_{\circlearrowleft} \to 0 \implies De_{rot} \to \infty \tag{95} \\ \Sigma \alpha_i^2 &= 3 - \frac{v_{tot}^2}{c^2} \tag{96} \\ v_{tot} &\to c \implies \Sigma \alpha_i^2 = 2 \tag{97} \\ \mathcal{L}_{dynamic} &= \frac{1}{2} \rho_{\tau} \Big[ \alpha_{\parallel}(\nabla h)^2 + \alpha_{\perp}(\nabla \times \mathbf{A})^2 + \alpha_{\circlearrowleft}(\nabla \times \mathbf{v}_{\psi})^2 \Big] - \frac{1}{2} \rho_{\tau} c^2 \tag{98} \\ \mathcal{L}_{kin} &= \frac{1}{2} \Big[ \alpha_{\parallel}(\nabla h)^2 + \alpha_{\perp}(\nabla \times \mathbf{A})^2 + \alpha_{\circlearrowleft}(\nabla \times \mathbf{v}_{\psi})^2 \Big] - \frac{1}{2} c^2 \tag{99} \\ \mathcal{L}_{kin}(v_{tot}, \theta, \phi) &= \frac{1}{2} v_{tot}^2 \Big[ \sqrt{1 - \frac{v_{tot}^2}{c^2} \cos^2(\theta)} \cos^2(\theta) \nonumber \\ &\quad + \sqrt{1 - \frac{v_{tot}^2}{c^2} \sin^2(\theta)\cos^2(\phi)} \sin^2(\theta)\cos^2(\phi) \nonumber \\ &\quad + \sqrt{1 - \frac{v_{tot}^2}{c^2} \sin^2(\theta)\sin^2(\phi)} \sin^2(\theta)\sin^2(\phi) \Big] \nonumber \\ &\quad - \frac{1}{2} c^2 \tag{100} \end{aligned}Equations (93) (94) (95) (96) (97) (98) (99) (100)

The Legendre Hamiltonian Translation

The continuous fluid dynamics evaluated by the Unified Lagrangian (ℒ𝛕=𝒦−𝒫\mathcal{L}_{\boldsymbol{\tau}} = \mathcal{K} - \mathcal{P}) dictate kinematic action. Extracting static topological observables requires translating the continuous system from velocity phase-space into momentum phase-space via the macroscopic Legendre transformation.

1. Macroscopic Conjugate Momentum:
The localized conjugate momentum density (𝐩macro\mathbf{p}_{macro}) evaluates as the partial derivative of the baseline Lagrangian with respect to the macroscopic driving fluid velocity (𝐯macro≡∇h\mathbf{v}_{macro} \equiv \nabla h). Because the structural potential energy density (𝒫\mathcal{P}) is independent of velocity, the derivative isolates the kinematic density: 𝐩macro=∂ℒ𝛕∂𝐯macro𝐩macro=∂∂𝐯macro(12ρτ𝐯macro2−12ρτc2)𝐩macro=ρτ𝐯macro\begin{aligned} \mathbf{p}_{macro} &= \frac{\partial \mathcal{L}_{\boldsymbol{\tau}}}{\partial \mathbf{v}_{macro}} \nonumber \\ \mathbf{p}_{macro} &= \frac{\partial}{\partial \mathbf{v}_{macro}} \left( \frac{1}{2} \rho_{\tau} \mathbf{v}_{macro}^2 - \frac{1}{2} \rho_{\tau} c^2 \right) \nonumber \\ \mathbf{p}_{macro} &= \rho_{\tau} \mathbf{v}_{macro} \tag{101} \end{aligned}Equation (101)

2. The Baseline Legendre Transform:
The baseline Hamiltonian density (ℋ𝛕\mathcal{H}_{\boldsymbol{\tau}}) evaluates as the Legendre transform of the Lagrangian, defined as the dot product of the macroscopic velocity and conjugate momentum minus the Lagrangian action: ℋ𝛕=𝐩macro⋅𝐯macro−ℒ𝛕ℋ𝛕=(ρτ𝐯macro)⋅𝐯macro−(𝒦macro−𝒫)ℋ𝛕=ρτ𝐯macro2−𝒦macro+𝒫\begin{aligned} \mathcal{H}_{\boldsymbol{\tau}} &= \mathbf{p}_{macro} \cdot \mathbf{v}_{macro} - \mathcal{L}_{\boldsymbol{\tau}} \nonumber \\ \mathcal{H}_{\boldsymbol{\tau}} &= (\rho_{\tau} \mathbf{v}_{macro}) \cdot \mathbf{v}_{macro} - (\mathcal{K}_{macro} - \mathcal{P}) \nonumber \\ \mathcal{H}_{\boldsymbol{\tau}} &= \rho_{\tau} \mathbf{v}_{macro}^2 - \mathcal{K}_{macro} + \mathcal{P} \nonumber \end{aligned} Because total macroscopic kinetic energy density is defined as 𝒦macro=12ρτ𝐯macro2\mathcal{K}_{macro} = \frac{1}{2}\rho_{\tau} \mathbf{v}_{macro}^2, the momentum term substitutes exactly as 2𝒦macro2\mathcal{K}_{macro}: ℋ𝛕=2𝒦macro−𝒦macro+𝒫ℋ𝛕=𝒦macro+𝒫\begin{aligned} \mathcal{H}_{\boldsymbol{\tau}} &= 2\mathcal{K}_{macro} - \mathcal{K}_{macro} + \mathcal{P} \nonumber \\ \mathcal{H}_{\boldsymbol{\tau}} &= \mathcal{K}_{macro} + \mathcal{P} \tag{102} \end{aligned}Equation (102)

3. The Covariant Bernoulli State:
Substituting the baseline kinetic and structural potential energy densities (𝒦macro=12ρτ𝐯macro2\mathcal{K}_{macro} = \frac{1}{2}\rho_{\tau} \mathbf{v}_{macro}^2 and 𝒫=12ρτc2\mathcal{P} = \frac{1}{2} \rho_{\tau} c^2) translates the continuous Lagrangian explicitly into the Bernoulli steady-state equation: ℋ𝛕=12ρτ[𝐯macro2+c2]\mathcal{H}_{\boldsymbol{\tau}} = \frac{1}{2} \rho_{\tau} \Big[ \mathbf{v}_{macro}^2 + c^2 \Big] \tag{103}Equation (103) The baseline energy state of the universe evaluates as the absolute sum of macroscopic dynamic pressure (12ρτ𝐯macro2\frac{1}{2}\rho_{\tau} \mathbf{v}_{macro}^2) and structural hydrostatic yield pressure (12ρτc2\frac{1}{2}\rho_{\tau} c^2).

4. Modal Energy Extraction (ℋdyn\mathcal{H}_{dyn} & ℋkin\mathcal{H}_{kin}):
To extract the dynamic energy state of a discrete topology, the Modal Admittances (αi\alpha_{i}) are applied to the geometric velocity fields. The Dynamic Hamiltonian (ℋdyn\mathcal{H}_{dyn}) sums the compliant kinetic strains and the structural potential: ℋdyn=12ρτ[α∥(∇h)2+α⟂(∇×𝐀)2+α↺(∇×𝐯ψ)2]+12ρτc2\mathcal{H}_{dyn} = \frac{1}{2} \rho_{\tau} \Big[ \alpha_{\parallel}(\nabla h)^2 + \alpha_{\perp}(\nabla \times \mathbf{A})^2 + \alpha_{\circlearrowleft}(\nabla \times \mathbf{v}_{\psi})^2 \Big] + \frac{1}{2} \rho_{\tau} c^2 \tag{104}Equation (104) To evaluate the geometric phase-space state (Specific Energy), the absolute mass density (ρτ\rho_{\tau}) is mathematically annihilated from the Hamiltonian. Dividing ℋdyn\mathcal{H}_{dyn} by ρτ\rho_{\tau} isolates the Kinematic Hamiltonian (ℋkin\mathcal{H}_{kin}) in native spatiotemporal dimensions (m2/s2\text{m}^2/\text{s}^2): ℋkin=12[α∥(∇h)2+α⟂(∇×𝐀)2+α↺(∇×𝐯ψ)2]+12c2\mathcal{H}_{kin} = \frac{1}{2} \Big[ \alpha_{\parallel}(\nabla h)^2 + \alpha_{\perp}(\nabla \times \mathbf{A})^2 + \alpha_{\circlearrowleft}(\nabla \times \mathbf{v}_{\psi})^2 \Big] + \frac{1}{2} c^2 \tag{105}Equation (105)

5. The Rotational Saturation Limit (ℋrest\mathcal{H}_{rest}):
Where the internal rotational velocity saturates the medium (|∇×𝐯ψ|→c|\nabla \times \mathbf{v}_{\psi}| \to c), the internal rotational admittance vanishes (α↺→0\alpha_{\circlearrowleft} \to 0).

Evaluating a saturated boundary at macroscopic rest (𝐯macro=0\mathbf{v}_{macro} = 0), the dynamic kinetic summation evaluates identically to zero. The Hamiltonian isolates to the absolute structural potential: ℋrest=12ρτc2\mathcal{H}_{rest} = \frac{1}{2} \rho_{\tau} c^2 \tag{106}Equation (106) The internal rotational energy evaluates as permanently frozen into the rest mass potential.

6. The Universal Angular Phase-Space Hamiltonian:
Defining the total velocity vtotv_{tot} via spherical coordinates extracts the geometric topology from the kinematic intensity (vtot2v_{tot}^2). Substituting the expanded angular components into the mass-independent Kinematic Hamiltonian (ℋkin\mathcal{H}_{kin}) yields: ℋkin(vtot,θ,ϕ)=12vtot2[α∥cos⁡2(θ)+α⟂sin⁡2(θ)cos⁡2(ϕ)+α↺sin⁡2(θ)sin⁡2(ϕ)]+12c2\begin{aligned} \mathcal{H}_{kin}(v_{tot}, \theta, \phi) = \frac{1}{2} v_{tot}^2 \Big[ &\alpha_{\parallel} \cos^2(\theta) + \alpha_{\perp} \sin^2(\theta)\cos^2(\phi) \nonumber \\ &+ \alpha_{\circlearrowleft} \sin^2(\theta)\sin^2(\phi) \Big] + \frac{1}{2} c^2 \tag{107} \end{aligned}Equation (107)

7. Topological Mass Extraction:
While kinematics evaluates as massless geometry, static topological observation requires coupling the geometry to the absolute baseline density (ρτ\rho_{\tau}).
